title: Longest and borrowed
description:
Write functions and a struct that hold references, with lifetimes.

```
longest("apple", "fig") = "apple"
first sentence: "Rust is fast."
highlight: [Rust] is fast. [Rust] is safe.
```
hints: The `'a` says the result lives no longer than both inputs, so the caller cannot keep it after either is dropped (lesson 4.04).
`text.split('.').next()` gives the first sentence without the dot; `text.find('.')` lets you keep it: `&text[..=i]`.
requirements: `struct Excerpt<'a> { part: &'a str }` built from the first sentence of a text, with `fn part(&self) -> &str`.
`fn find_all<'a>(text: &'a str, word: &str) -> Vec<&'a str>` returns slices of `text` (the second argument does not need `'a`).
stretch: Write `fn split_pair<'a>(s: &'a str, sep: char) -> Option<(&'a str, &'a str)>` and use it to read `key=value` lines.
